Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: In order to determine the Young's Modulus of a wire of radius 0.2 cm (measured using a scale of least count = 0.001 cm) and length 1m (measured using a scale of least count = 1 mm), a weight of mass 1 kg (measured using a scale of least count = 1 g) was hanged to get the elongation of 0.5 cm (measured using a scale of least count 0.001 cm). What will be the fractional error in the value of Young's Modulus determined by this experiment?
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
\Delta Y \over Y = ( \Delta m \over m \) + ( \Delta g \over g \) + ( \Delta A \over A \) + ( \Delta l \over l \) + ( \Delta L \over L \)

= ( 1g \over 1kg \) + 0 + 2( \Delta r \over r \) + ( \Delta l \over l \) + ( \Delta L \over L \)

= ( 1g \over 1kg \) + 2( 0.001cm \over 0.2cm \) + ( 0.001cm \over 0.5cm \) + ( 0.001m \over 1m \)

= ( 1 \over 1000 \) + 2( 1 × 10 \over 2 × 10^3 \) + ( 1 \over 5 × 10^2 \over 10^3 \) + ( 1 \over 10^3 \)

= 1 \over 1000 + 1 \over 100 + 2 \over 10^3 + 1 \over 10^3

= 1 + 10 + 2 + 1 \over 1000 = 14 \over 1000 × 100\%

= 1.4\%
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: A torque meter is calibrated to reference standards of mass, length and time each with 5 \% accuracy. After calibration, the measured torque with this torque meter will have net accuracy of :

We know that, torque applied on a rotating body,

\beginaligned \tau &= Force × Perpendicular distance \\\\ \Rightarrow \quad[\tau] &=\left[MLT^-2\][L] \Rightarrow[\tau]=\left[ML^2 T^-2\] \endaligned \Rightarrow \Delta \tau \over \tau = \Delta M \over M + 2\Delta L \over L + 2\Delta T \over T = 5 × 5\% = 25\%

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question:
Match List - I with List - II.

table width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; table, th, td border: 1px solid black; th, td padding: 10px; -align: center; th background-color: blue; color: white; List I (Number) List II (Significant figure) (A) 1001 (I) 3 (B) 010.1 (II) 4 (C) 100.100 (III) 5 (D) 0.0010010 (IV) 6
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Significant figures in a number represent the digits that carry meaning contributing to its precision. This includes all digits except:
  • All leading zeros.

  • Trailing zeros only when they are merely placeholders to indicate the scale of the number (they must not be significant if there is no decimal point).
Here is the explanation for the significant figures of each number in List I: (A) 1001 - All the digits in this number are significant because there are no leading or trailing zeros acting as placeholders. Hence, this number has 4 significant figures. (B) 010.1 - The leading zero is not significant, but the zero between 1 and the decimal point, the 1 itself, and the 1 after the decimal point are all significant. So, this number has 3 significant figures. (C) 100.100 - Here, the number has zeros which are significant since they are between significant digits or after the decimal point. This makes all the zeros and the 1s significant. Therefore, the number has 6 significant figures. (D) 0.0010010 - The leading zeros are not significant, but the three zeros within and at the end of the number are significant because they are between significant digits or at the end of the number after the decimal. Therefore, this number has 5 significant figures. Given List I and List II, the correct matching based on the explanation of significant figures is as follows: Option A (A) - II (1001 has 4 significant figures) (B) - I (010.1 has 3 significant figures) (C) - IV (100.100 has 6 significant figures) (D) - III (0.0010010 has 5 significant figures) Thus, the correct answer is Option A.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: The measured value of the length of a simple pendulum is 20 cm with 2 mm accuracy. The time for 50 oscillations was measured to be 40 seconds with 1 second resolution. From these measurements, the accuracy in the measurement of acceleration due to gravity is N \%. The value of N is:
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: \beginaligned & T=2 \pi \sqrt\frac\ellg \\ & g=\frac₄ \pi^2 \ellT^2 \\ & \frac\Delta gg=\frac\Delta \ell\ell+\frac₂ \Delta TT \\ & =\frac₀.220+2(\frac₁₄₀\) \\ & =\frac₁.220 \endaligned Percentage change =\frac₁.220 × 100=6 \%

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: A physical quantity Q is found to depend on quantities a, b, c by the relation Q=\fraca^4 b^3c^2. The percentage error in a, b and c are 3 \%, 4 \% and 5 \% respectively. Then, the percentage error in Q is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: \beginaligned & Q=\fraca^4 b^3c^2 \\ & \frac\Delta QQ=4 \frac\Delta aa+3 \frac\Delta bb+2 \frac\Delta cc \endaligned \frac\Delta QQ × 100=4(\frac\Delta aa × 100\)+3(\frac\Delta bb × 100\)+2(\frac\Delta cc × 100\) \beginaligned \% error in Q & =4 × 3 \%+3 × 4 \%+2 × 5 \% \\ & =12 \%+12 \%+10 \% \\ & =34 \% \endaligned

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: screw gauge with a pitch of 0.5 mm and a circular scale with 50 divisions is used to measure the thickness of a thin sheet of Aluminium. Before starting the measurement, it is found that when the two jaws of the screw gauge are brought in contact, the 45<sup>th</sup> division coincides with the main scale line and that the zero of the main scale is barely visible. What is the thickness of the sheet if the main scale reading is 0.5 mm and the 25<sup>th</sup> division coincides with the main scale line?
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Least count = 0.5 \over 50 = 0.01 mm

Zero error = (45 - 50) × 0.01 mm = - 0.05 mm

Thickness of sheet = (0.5 + 25 × 0.01) - (-0.05)

= 0.50 + 0.30 = 0.80 mm

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: The pitch of the screw gauge is 1 mm and there are 100 divisions on the circular scale. When nothing is put in between the jaws, the zero of the circular scale lies 8 divisions below the reference line. When a wire is placed between the jaws, the first linear scale division is clearly visible while 72<sup>nd</sup> division on circular scale coincides with the reference line. The radius of the wire is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:

zero error = + 8 × LC = + 0.08 mm

True reading (Diameter)

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: A screw gauge of pitch 0.5 mm is used to measure the diameter of uniform wire of length 6.8 cm, the main scale reading is 1.5 mm and circular scale reading is 7 . The calculated curved surface area of wire to appropriate significant figures is : [Screw gauge has 50 divisions on its circular scale]

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: While measuring diameter of wire using screw gauge the following readings were noted. Main scale reading is 1 mm and circular scale reading is equal to 42 divisions. Pitch of screw gauge is 1 mm and it has 100 divisions on circular scale. The diameter of the wire is \fracx₅₀ mm. The value of x is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
To determine the diameter of the wire using a screw gauge, we employ the formula: Total reading = MSR + (CSR × LC) where:
  • MSR (Main Scale Reading) is the value read directly from the main scale in mm.

  • CSR (Circular Scale Reading) is the number of divisions observed on the circular scale.

  • LC (Least Count) is the value of one division on the circular scale, calculated as \fracPitchNumber of divisions on the circular scale.
Given:
  • Main Scale Reading (MSR) = 1 mm

  • Circular Scale Reading (CSR) = 42 divisions

  • Pitch of screw gauge = 1 mm

  • Number of divisions on circular scale = 100
First, we find the Least Count (LC): LC = \fracPitchNumber of divisions on the circular scale = \frac₁ mm₁₀₀ = 0.01 mm Then we calculate the total measurement of the diameter of the wire: Total reading = MSR + (CSR × LC) = 1 mm + (42 × 0.01 mm) = 1 mm + 0.42 mm = 1.42 mm Given that the diameter of the wire is also represented as \fracx₅₀ mm, we can equate this to our found total reading: 1.42 mm = \fracx₅₀ mm Solving for x: 1.42 = \fracx₅₀ x = 1.42 × 50 x = 71 Therefore, the value of x is 71, which corresponds to Option B: 71.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: Velocity (v) and acceleration (a) in two systems of units 1 and 2 are related as v_2 = n \over m^2v_1 and a_2 = a_1 \over mn respectively. Here m and n are constants. The relations for distance and time in two systems respectively are :

options.A: N^3 \over m^3L_1 = L_2 and n^2 \over mT_1 = T_2
options.B: L_1 = n^4 \over m^2L_2 and T_1 = n^2 \over mT_2
options.C: L_1 = n^2 \over mL_2 and T_1 = n^4 \over m^2T_2
options.D: N^2 \over mL_1 = L_2 and n^4 \over m^2T_1 = T_2

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: [L] = [v^2] \over [a] so [v_2]^2 \over [a_2] = \left[ n \over m^2v_1 \]^2 \over \left[ a_1 \over mn \] [v_2]^2 \over [a_2] = n^3 \over m^3[v_1]^2 \over [a_1] or [L_2] = n^3 \over m^3[L_1] Similarly, [T] = [v] \over [a] So, [T_2] = n^2 \over m[T_1]
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: The least count of the main scale of a vernier callipers is 1 mm. Its vernier scale is divided into 10 divisions and coincide with 9 divisions of the main scale. When jaws are touching each other, the 7<sup>th</sup> division of vernier scale coincides with a division of main scale and the zero of vernier scale is lying side of the zero of main scale. When this vernier is used to measure length of a cylinder the zero of the vernier scale between 3.1 cm and 3.2 cm and 4<sup>th</sup> VSD coincides with a main scale division. The length of the cylinder is : (VSD is vernier scale division)
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: If n main scale divisions coincide with (n + 1) vernier scale divisions. The least count of vernier callipers, when each centimetre on the main scale is divided into five equal parts, will be :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: 5 parts of main scale division = 1 cm \therefore 1 part of main scale division = 1 \over 5 cm \therefore 1 M.S.D. = 1 \over 5 cm (n + 1) vernier scale division = n main scale division. \therefore 1 V.S.D. = n \over n+1 M.S.D. = n \over n+1 × 1 M.S.D. = n \over n + 1 × 1 \over 5 cm We know, L.C. = 1 M.S.D. - 1 V,S.D. = 1 \over 5 cm - n \over 5(n + 1) cm = n + 1 - n \over 5(n + 1) cm = 1 \over 5(n + 1) cm
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: In a Vernier Calipers, 10 divisions of Vernier scale is equal to the 9 divisions of main scale. When both jaws of Vernier calipers touch each other, the zero of the Vernier scale is shifted to the left of zero of the main scale and 4^ th Vernier scale division exactly coincides with the main scale reading. One main scale division is equal to 1 mm. While measuring diameter of a spherical body, the body is held between two jaws. It is now observed that zero of the Vernier scale lies between 30 and 31 divisions of main scale reading and 6^ th Vernier scale division exactly coincides with the main scale reading. The diameter of the spherical body will be :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Given, In Vernier calipers, 10 VSD =9 MSD

\Rightarrow \quad 1 VSD =\frac₉₁₀ MSD

\therefore Least count of vernier scale,

\beginaligned LC &=1 MSD-1 VSD \\\\ &=1 MSD-\frac₉₁₀ MSD=\operatornameMSD(1-\frac₉₁₀\) \\\\ &=\frac MSD 10=\frac₁ mm₁₀ \quad[\because 1 MSD=1 mm] \\\\ &=0.1 mm=0.01 cm \endaligned

According to given situation,

Negative error = Main scale reading - Least count × Number of coinciding main scale division

=0.1-0.01 × 4=0.1-0.04=0.06 cm

\therefore Diameter of spherical body

\beginaligned &=30 × 0.1+6 × 0.01+0.06 \\\\ &=3.0+0.06+0.06=3.12 cm \endaligned

Which is closest to 3.10 cm.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: 10 divisions on the main scale of a Vernier calliper coincide with 11 divisions on the Vernier scale. If each division on the main scale is of 5 units, the least count of the instrument is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: The least count of a Vernier caliper is the smallest measurement that can be obtained with it and is determined by the difference in the measurement of one main scale division and one Vernier scale division. In this case, 10 divisions on the main scale coincide with 11 divisions on the Vernier scale. This means that 11 divisions on the Vernier scale are equal in length to 10 divisions on the main scale. Since each division on the main scale is 5 units, this is equal to: 10 divisions on main scale × 5 units per division = 50 units The length of 10 divisions on the main scale (or 50 units) is therefore equal to the length of 11 divisions on the Vernier scale. This means that: 1 division on the Vernier scale = \frac₅₀ units₁₁ Therefore, the least count of the Vernier caliper, which is the difference between one division on the main scale and one division on the Vernier scale, can be calculated as follows: Least count = value of one main scale division - value of one Vernier scale division Least count = 5 units - \frac₅₀ units₁₁ Least count = \frac₅₅ units₁₁ - \frac₅₀ units₁₁ Least count = \frac₅ units₁₁ Thus, the least count of the Vernier caliper is \frac₅ units₁₁ Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A: \frac₅₁₁
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: Least count of a vernier caliper is \frac₁₂₀ N cm. The value of one division on the main scale is 1 mm. Then the number of divisions of main scale that coincide with N divisions of vernier scale is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: In a vernier caliper, the least count is the smallest distance measurable by the instrument. It can be defined using the difference between one main scale division and one vernier scale division. Given the least count, we can relate the number of divisions on the main scale to the divisions on the vernier scale. The given least count of the vernier caliper is: \frac₁₂₀ N cm We know that the value of one division on the main scale is: 1 mm To find the number of divisions on the main scale that coincide with N divisions of the vernier scale, let\u₂₀₁₉s denote: The number of divisions on the main scale = M The number of divisions on the vernier scale = N The least count formula for a vernier caliper is given by: Least Count = Value of one main scale division - Value of one vernier scale division The value of one main scale division is: 1 mm The value of one vernier scale division can be expressed in terms of the number of divisions M and N: Value of one vernier scale division = \fracMN mm Given the least count: \frac₁₂₀ N cm = \frac₁₂₀ N · 10 mm = \frac₁₂ N mm Using the least count formula, we have: \frac₁₂ N = 1 - \fracMN Rearranging the equation to solve for the number of main scale divisions (M), we get: 1 - \frac₁₂ N = \fracMN Simplifying further: \frac₂ N - 12 N = \fracMN Multiplying both sides by N, we get the value of M: M = \frac₂ N - 12 Therefore, the correct answer is option D: ( \frac₂ N - 12 \)
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: In a vernier calliper, when both jaws touch each other, zero of the vernier scale shifts towards left and its 4^ th division coincides exactly with a certain division on main scale. If₅₀ vernier scale divisions equal to 49 main scale divisions and zero error in the instrument is 0.04 mm then how many main scale divisions are there in 1 cm ?
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: \beginaligned & 0.04=4( L. C.) \\ & \Rightarrow L.C =0.01 mm \\ & \beginarrayl 1 MSD-\frac₄₉₅₀ MS D=0.01 mm \\ \Rightarrow 1 MSD=50 × 0.01 mm \\ \quad=0.5 mm \\ \Rightarrow 1 cm=20(0.5 mm) \endarray \endaligned
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: In finding out refractive index of glass slab the following observations were made through travelling microscope 50 vernier scale division =49 MSD ; 20 divisions on main scale in each cm For mark on paper MSR =8.45 cm, VC=26 For mark on paper seen through slab MSR=7.12 cm, VC=41 For powder particle on the top surface of the glass slab MSR =4.05 cm, VC=1 (MSR = Main Scale Reading, VC = Vernier Coincidence) Refractive index of the glass slab is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
To find the refractive index of the glass slab, we first need to calculate the actual readings using the Main Scale Reading (MSR) and Vernier Coincidence (VC), and understand how to translate these values into a measurement of the refractive index. We will start by calculating the Least Count (LC) of the vernier calipers. The least count (LC) of the traveling microscope is given by the formula: LC = MSD - VSD Where MSD is the value of one main scale division and VSD is the value of one vernier scale division in terms of the main scale. We are told 50 vernier scale divisions equal 49 main scale divisions (MSD), so 1 VSD is \frac₄₉₅₀ of an MSD. Given that 20 divisions on the main scale represent 1 cm, each main scale division (MSD) represents: 1 \, MSD = \frac₁ \, cm₂₀ = 0.05 \, cm Therefore, the least count (LC) of the microscope is: LC = 0.05 \, cm - ( \frac₄₉₅₀ × 0.05 \, cm \) = 0.05 \, cm - 0.049 \, cm = 0.001 \, cm Now, using the least count to find the total reading (TR) from both supplied observations:
  1. For the mark on paper, the total reading (TR) is:
TR = MSR + (VC × LC) TR_paper = 8.45 \, cm + (26 × 0.001 \, cm) = 8.45 \, cm + 0.026 \, cm = 8.476 \, cm
  1. For the mark on the paper seen through the slab, the total reading is:
TR_seen through slab = 7.12 \, cm + (41 × 0.001 \, cm) = 7.12 \, cm + 0.041 \, cm = 7.161 \, cm
  1. For the powder particle on the top surface of the glass slab:
TR_top surface = 4.05 \, cm + (1 × 0.001 \, cm) = 4.05 \, cm + 0.001 \, cm = 4.051 \, cm The real depth (RD) observed directly is the difference between the first and third observations (mark on paper and powder particle on top surface): RD = TR_paper - TR_top surface = 8.476 \, cm - 4.051 \, cm = 4.425 \, cm The apparent depth (AD) when viewed through the slab is the difference between the second and third observations: AD = TR_seen through slab - TR_top surface = 7.161 \, cm - 4.051 \, cm = 3.11 \, cm The refractive index (n) of the glass slab can be found using the formula: n = \fracReal Depth (RD)Apparent Depth (AD) = \frac₄.425 \, cm₃.11 \, cm Calculating this gives: n = \frac₄.4253.11 \approx 1.42 Therefore, the refractive index of the glass slab is approximately 1.42, which corresponds to Option D.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: If two vectors \overarrow P = \widehat i + 2m\widehat j + m\widehat k and \overarrow Q = 4\widehat i - 2\widehat j + m\widehat k are perpendicular to each other. Then, the value of m will be :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
\vecP \,\&\, \vecQ are perpendicular

\beginaligned & \overarrowP · \overarrowQ=0 \\\\ & (\hati+2 m \hatj+m \hatk) ·(4 \hati-2 \hatj+m \hatk)=0 \\\\ & \Rightarrow 4-4 m+m^2=0 \\\\ & \Rightarrow(m-2)^2=0 \Rightarrow m=2 \endaligned
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question:
Statement I :

Two forces ( \overarrow P + \overarrow Q \) and ( \overarrow P - \overarrow Q \) where \overarrow P \bot \overarrow Q , when act at an angle \theta1 to each other, the magnitude of their resultant is \sqrt 3(P^2 + Q^2) , when they act at an angle \theta2, the magnitude of their resultant becomes \sqrt 2(P^2 + Q^2) . This is possible only when \theta _1 < \theta _2.

Statement II :

In the situation given above.

\theta1 = 60^\circ and \theta2 = 90^\circ

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :-

options.A: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
\overarrow A = \overarrow P + \overarrow Q

\overarrow B = \overarrow P - \overarrow Q

\overarrow P \bot \overarrow Q

\left| \overarrow A \| = \left| \overarrow B \| = \sqrt 2(P^2 + Q^2)(1 + \cos \theta )

For \left| \overarrow A + \overarrow B \| = \sqrt 3(P^2 + Q^2)

\theta _1 = 60^\circ

For \left| \overarrow A + \overarrow B \| = \sqrt 2(P^2 + Q^2)

\theta _2 = 90^\circ
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: When vector \vecA=2 \hati+3 \hatj+2 \hatk is subtracted from vector \overarrowB, it gives a vector equal to 2 \hatj. Then the magnitude of vector \overarrowB will be :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Given that when vector \vecA=2 \hati+3 \hatj+2 \hatk is subtracted from vector \overarrowB, it gives a vector equal to 2 \hatj.

We can write this as:

\vecB - \vecA = 2 \hatj

Now, let's express the vector \overarrowB in terms of its components:

\vecB = B_x \hati + B_y \hatj + B_z \hatk

Subtract vector \vecA from vector \vecB:

(B_x \hati + B_y \hatj + B_z \hatk) - (2 \hati+3 \hatj+2 \hatk) = 2 \hatj

Comparing the components, we get:

B_x - 2 = 0 \\ B_y - 3 = 2 \\ B_z - 2 = 0

Solving these equations, we find the components of vector \vecB:

B_x = 2 \\ B_y = 5 \\ B_z = 2

Now, we can find the magnitude of vector \vecB:

|\vecB| = \sqrtB_x^2 + B_y^2 + B_z^2 = \sqrt₂^2 + 5^2 + 2^2 = \sqrt₄ + 25 + 4 = \sqrt₃₃

Therefore, the magnitude of vector \overarrowB is \sqrt₃₃
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: Two forces having magnitude A and \fracA₂ are perpendicular to each other. The magnitude of their resultant is:
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: The resultant of two perpendicular vectors is given by the Pythagorean theorem. If we have two vectors of magnitudes A and \fracA₂, the resultant R is: R = \sqrtA^2 + (\fracA₂\)^2 = \sqrtA^2 + \fracA^24 = \sqrt\frac₅A^24 = \frac\sqrt₅ A₂.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: In an experiment to determine the period of a simple pendulum of length 1 m, it is attached to different spherical bobs of radii r<sub>1</sub> and r<sub>2</sub> . The two spherical bobs have uniform mass distribution. If the relative difference in the periods, is found to be 5×10<sup>−4</sup> s, the difference in radii, \left| \.r<sub>1</sub> - r<sub>2</sub> \left| \. is best given by :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: The time period is given by the formula T = 2\pi \sqrt l \over g which clearly indicates that the time period is directly proportional to the length of the pendulum l, that is, T \propto \sqrt l Here, l = 1 m. Therefore, \Delta T \over l = 1 \over 2\Delta l \over l ....... (1) where \Delta l = \left| r_1 - r_2 \|. Substituting the values in Eq. (1), we get 5 × 10^ - 4 = 1 \over 2( r_1 - r_2 \over 1 \) \Rightarrow r_1 - r_2 = 10 × 10^ - 4 = 10^ - 3 m = 10^ - 1 cm = 0.1 cm
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question:
standing wave is formed by the superposition of two waves travelling in opposite directions. The transverse displacement is given by

y(x, t) = 0.5 sin ( 5\pi \over 4x \)\, cos(200 \pi t).

What is the speed of the travelling wave moving in the positive x direction ?

(x and t are in meter and second, respectively.)
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Standard equation of standing wave,

y(x, t) = 2a sin kx cos \omega t

Given,

y(x, t) = 0.5 sin ( 5\pi \over 4x \) cos (200\pi t).

So, k = 5\pi \over 4 and \omega = 200\pi

\therefore\,\,\, Speed of travelling wave

= \omega \over k = 200\pi \over 5\pi \over 4 = 160 m/s.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: heavy ball of mass M is suspendeed from the ceiling of a car by a light string of mass m (m < < M). When the car is at rest, the speed of transverse waves in the string is 60 ms<sup>-1</sup>. When the car has acceleration a, the wave-speed increases to 60.5 ms<sup>-1</sup>. The value of a, in terms of gravitational acceleration g, is closest to :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Resultant force on the ball of mass M when car is moving with a acceleration a is ,

Fnet = \sqrt ( Mg \)^2 + ( Ma \)^2

= M\sqrt g^2 + a^2

\therefore T = M\sqrt g^2 + a^2

We know,

Velocity, V = \sqrt T \over \mu

When Car is at rest then,

60 = \sqrt Mg \over \mu . . . . (1)

and when is moving then

60.5 = \sqrt M\sqrt g^2 + a^2 \over \mu . . . . (2)

By dividing (2) by (1) we get,

60.5 \over 60 = \sqrt \sqrt g^2 + a^2 \over g

\Rightarrow ( 1 + 0.5 \over 60 \) = ( g^2 + a^2 \over g^2 \)^1 \over 4

\Rightarrow g^2 + a^2 \over g^2 = ( 1 + 0.5 \over 60 \)^4

\Rightarrow g^2 + a^2 \over g^2 = 1 + 4 × 0.5 \over 60 [Using Binomial approximation]

\Rightarrow g^2 + a^2 \over g^2 = 1 + 1 \over 30

\Rightarrow 1 + a^2 \over g^2 = 1 + 1 \over 30

\Rightarrow a \over g = 1 \over \sqrt 30

\Rightarrow a = g \over \sqrt 30

\therefore Closest answer, a = g \over 5
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: Assume that the displacement(s) of air is proportional to the pressure difference (\Delta p) created by a sound wave. Displacement (s) further depends on the speed of sound (v), density of air (\rho ) and the frequency (f). If \Delta p 10 Pa, v 300 m/s, \rho 1 kg/m<sup>3</sup> and f 1000 Hz, then s will be of the order of (take the multiplicative constant to be 1) :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Given, S \propto \Delta p

and Proportionally constant = 1

We know,

\Delta p = S\beta k

= \rho v2 × \omega \over v × S

= \rho v\omega S

\therefore S = \Delta p \over \rho v\omega

= \Delta p \over \rho v₂\pi f

= \Delta p \over \rho vf

[As Proportionally constant = 1 so assume 2\pi = 1]

= 10 \over 1 × 300 × 1000

= 1 \over 30mm

\approx 3 \over 100mm
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: uniform thin rope of length 12 m and mass 6 kg hangs vertically from a rigid support and a block of mass 2 kg is attached to its free end. A transverse short wavetrain of wavelength 6 cm is produced at the lower end of the rope. What is the wavelength of the wavetrain (in cm) when it reaches the top of the rope ?
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
T1 = 2g

T2 = 8g

V = \sqrt T \over \mu

\therefore V \propto \sqrt T

Also V = f\lambda

\therefore V1 = f1\lambda 1

and V2 = f2\lambda 2

We know frequency of sources are same.

\therefore f1 = f2

So \sqrt T_1 \over T_2 = \lambda _1 \over \lambda _2

\Rightarrow \sqrt 2g \over 8g = 6 \over \lambda _2

\Rightarrow \lambda 2 = 12 cm
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: sound wave of frequency 245 Hz travels with the speed of 300 ms<sup>-1</sup> along the positive x-axis. Each point of the wave moves to and from through a total distance of 6 cm. What will be the mathematical expression of this travelling wave?
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Y = A\sin (kx - \omega t)

A = 6 \over 2 = 3cm = 0.03 m

\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi × 245

\omega = 1.5 × 10^3

k = \omega \over v = 1.5 × 10^3 \over 300

k = 5.1

y = 0.03\sin (5.1x - (1.5 × 10^3)t)
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: If a wave gets refracted into a denser medium, then which of the following is true?

options.B: Wavelength increases, sped decreases and frequency remains constant.
options.C: Wavelength and speed decreases but frequency remains constant.

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: Frequency is independent of medium. For denser medium, wavelength and speed both would decrease.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: In the wave equation y=0.5 \sin \frac₂ \pi\lambda(400 t-x) \,m the velocity of the wave will be:
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: v_wave = \left| coefficient\,of\,t \over coefficient\,of\,x \| = 400 \over 1 = 400 m/s
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: train is moving on a straight track with speed 20\,ms^ - 1. It is blowing its whistle at the frequency of 1000 Hz. The percentage change in the frequency heard by a person standing near the track as the train passes him is (speed of sound = 320\,ms^ - 1) close to :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
f_1 = f\left[ v \over v - v_s \] = f × 320 \over 300Hz

f_2 = f\left[ v \over v + v_s \] = f × 320 \over 340Hz

( f_2 \over f_1 - 1 \) × 100 = ( 300 \over 340 - 1 \) × 100 = 12\%
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: Two engines pass each other moving in opposite directions with uniform speed of 30 m/s. One of them is blowing a whistle of frequency 540 Hz. Calculate the frequency heard by driver of second engine before they pass each other. Speed of sound is 330 m/sec :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Frequency heard by the driver of second engine,

F' = ( v + v_0 \over v - v_S \) f

given v0 = vs = 30 m/s

\therefore f' = ( 330 + 30 \over 330 - 30 \) × 540

= 648 Hz
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question:
Two cars A and B are moving away from each other in opposite directions. Both the cars are moving with a speed of 20 ms\–1 with respect to the ground. If an observer in car A detects a frequency 2000 Hz of the sound coming from car B, what is the natural frequency of the sound source in car B ?
(speed of sound in air = 340 ms\–1) :-
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
f = ( v \pm u_0 \) \over ( v \pm u_s \).f_0 = ( v - 20 \) \over ( v + 20 \).f_0

\Rightarrow 2000 = 320 \over 360.f_0

\Rightarrow 2000 × 9 \over 8 = f_0 = 2250\,Hz
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: driver in a car, approaching a vertical wall notices that the frequency of his car horn, has changed from 440 Hz to 480 Hz, when it gets reflected from the wall. If the speed of sound in air is 345 m/s, then the speed of the car is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
f1 = frequency heard by wall
= ( v_s - 0 \over v_s - v_c \)f_0 = v_s \over v_s - v_c × 440

f2 = frequency heard by driver after reflection from wall

= ( v_s + v_c \over v_s - 0 \)f_1

\Rightarrow 480 = ( v_s + v_c \over v_s \)f_1

\Rightarrow 480 = ( v_s + v_c \over v_s \)( v_s \over v_s - v_c \) × 440

\Rightarrow 480 = ( v_s + v_c \over v_s - v_c \) × 440

\Rightarrow 480 = ( 345 + v_c \over 345 - v_c \) × 440

\Rightarrow 12 = ( 345 + v_c \over 345 - v_c \) × 11

\Rightarrow 11 × 345 + 11vc = 12 × 345 – 12vc

\Rightarrow vc = 345 \over 23 m/s = 345 \over 23 × 18 \over 5 = 54 km/hr
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: stationary observer receives sound from two identical tuning forks, one of which approaches and the other one recedes with the same speed (much less than the speed of sound). The observer hears 2 beats/sec. The oscillation frequency of each tuning fork is v<sub>0</sub> = 1400 Hz and the velocity of sound in air is 350 m/s. The speed of each tuning fork is close to :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
f1 = ( c \over c - v \)f_0

f1 = ( c \over c + v \)f_0

beat frequency = f1 \– f2

= cf_0( 1 \over c - v - 1 \over c + v \)

= cf_0( 2v \over c^2 - v^2 \)

As c \gg v then c^2 - v^2 = c^2

= cf_0( 2v \over c^2 \)

= f_0( 2v \over c \)

\therefore f_0( 2v \over c \) = 2

\Rightarrow v = 350 \over 1400 = 1 \over 4 m/s
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: The driver of a bus approaching a big wall notices that the frequency of his bus's horn changes from 420 Hz to 490 Hz when he hears it after it gets reflected from the wall. Find the speed of the bus if speed of the sound is 330 ms<sup>\–1</sup>.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Frequency received by wall,

f_w = ( 330 \over 330 - v \)f_0

Frequency after reflection, f' = ( 330 + v \over 330 \)f_w

= ( 330 + v \over 330 \) × ( 330 \over 330 - v \)f_0

\Rightarrow 490 = ( 330 + v \over 330 - v \)₄₂₀

\therefore v = 25.2 m/s

= 91 km/h
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: A person observes two moving trains, 'A' reaching the station and 'B' leaving the station with equal speed of 30 m / s. If both trains emit sounds with frequency 300 Hz, (Speed of sound: 330 m / s) approximate difference of frequencies heard by the person will be:
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
By doppler effect : f^\prime=f_0\left[\fracv-v_0v-v_s\]

\Rightarrow \quad f_A^\prime=300\left[\frac₃₃₀₃₃₀-30\] Hz

=330 Hz

And f_B^\prime=300\left[\frac₃₃₀₃₃₀+30\] Hz

=\frac₅₆ × 330 Hz=275 Hz

\therefore \Delta f=330-275=55 Hz.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: resonance tube is old and has jagged end. It is still used in the laboratory to determine velocity of sound in air. A tuning fork of frequency 512 Hz produces first resonance when the tube is filled with water to a mark 11 cm below a reference mark, near the open end of the tube. The experiment is repeated with another fork of frequency 256 Hz which produces first resonance when water reaches a mark 27 cm below the reference mark. The velocity of sound in air, obtained in the experiment, is close to :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: In first resonance, length of air column = \lambda \over 4. So, l_1 + e = \lambda \over 4 or 11 × 4 + 4e = \lambda So, speed of sound is \Rightarrow v = f_1\lambda = 512(44 + 4e) ...... (i) And in second case, l'_1 + e = \lambda ' \over 4 or 27 × 4 + 4e = \lambda ' \Rightarrow v = f_2\lambda ' = 256(108 + 4e) ..... (ii) Dividing both Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get 1 = 512(44 + 4e) \over 256(108 + 4e) \Rightarrow e = 5 cm Substituting value of e in Eq. (i), we get Speed of sound v = 512(44 + 4e) = 512(44 + 4 × 5) = 512 × 64 cm s-1 = 327.68 ms-1 \approx 328 ms-1
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: person trying to lose weight by burning fat lifts a mass of 10 kg upto a height of 1 m 1000 times. Assume that the potential energy lost each time he lowers the mass is dissipated. How much fat will he use up considering the work done only when the weight is lifted up? Fat supplies 3.8 × 10^7J of energy per kg which is converted to mechanical energy with a 20\% efficiency rate. Take g = 9.8\,ms^ - 2 :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Assume the amount of fat is used = x kg

So total Mechanical energy available through fat

= x × 3.8 × 10^7 × 20 \over 100

And work done through lifting up

= 10 × 9.8 × 1000 = 98000 J

\Rightarrow x × 3.8 × 10^7 × 20 \over 100 = 98000

\Rightarrow x = 12.89 × 10-3 kg
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: time dependent force F = 6t acts on a particle of mass 1 kg. If the particle starts from rest, the work done by the force during the first 1 sec. will be:
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Given that, F = 6t

We know, F = ma = mdv \over dt

\therefore mdv \over dt = 6t

\Rightarrow 1.dv \over dt = 6t [as m = 1]

\Rightarrow \int\limits_0^v dv = \int 6t dt

\Rightarrow v = 6\left[ t^2 \over 2 \]_0^1

\Rightarrow v = 6 \over 2 = 3 m/s [ as given t = 1 sec ]

Work done by the body during the first 1 form work-energy theorem,

W = \Delta K.E = 1 \over 2m( V^2 - v^2 \)

= 1 \over 2.1.( 3^2 - 0^2 \) = 4.5 J
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: particle is moving in a circular path of radius a under the action of an attractive potential U = - k \over 2r^2 Its total energy is:
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
We know, Total energy = Kinetic energy + Potential energy

Potential energy given as U = - k \over 2r^2

We need to find Kinetic Energy.

As Force acting on the particle (F) = - dU \over dr

\Rightarrow F = - d \over dr( - k \over 2r^2 \)

= k \over 2 × ( - 2 \) × r^ - 3

= - k \over r^3

Because of this force particle is having circular motion so it will provide possible centripetal force.

\left| F \| = mv^2 \over r

\Rightarrow mv^2 \over r = k \over r^3

\Rightarrow mv^2 = k \over r^2

We know kinetic energy of particle, K = 1 \over 2mv^2 = k \over 2r^2

As Total energy = Kinetic energy + Potential energy

So Total energy = k \over 2r^2 - k \over 2r^2 = 0
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: force acts on a 2 kg object so that its position is given as a function of time as x = 3t<sup>2</sup> + 5. What is the work done by this force in first 5 seconds ?
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Displacement,

x = 3t2 + 5

\therefore v = dx \over dt = 6t

At t = 0, velocity = 6 × 0 = 0

at t = 5, velocity = 5 × 6 = 30 m/s

we know from work energy theorem,

Work (W) = change in kinetic energy (\Delta K)

= 1 \over 2mv_F^2 - 1 \over 2mv_i^2

= 1 \over 2 × 2 × (30)2 - 0

= 900 J
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: particle which is experiencing a force, given by \overarrow F = 3\widehat i - 12\widehat j, undergoes a displacement of \overarrow d = 4\overarrow i particle had a kinetic energy of 3 J at the beginning of the displacement, what is its kinetic energy at the end of the displacement ?
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Work done = \overarrow F · \overarrow d

= 12 J

work energy theorem

wnet = \Delta K.E.

12 = Kf - 3

Kf = 15 J
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: boy is rolling a 0.5 kg ball on the frictionless floor with the speed of 20 ms<sup>-1</sup>. The ball gets deflected by an obstacle on the way. After deflection it moves with 5% of its initial kinetic energy. What is the speed of the ball now?
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
K.E._f = 5\% \,KE_i

1 \over 2mv^2 = 5 \over 100 × 1 \over 2 × m × 20^2

v^2 = 1 \over 20 × 20^2 = 20

v = \sqrt 20 = 2\sqrt 5 m/s

= 4.47 m/s
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: block moving horizontally on a smooth surface with a speed of 40 m/s splits into two parts with masses in the ratio of 1 : 2. If the smaller part moves at 60 m/s in the same direction, then the fractional change in kinetic energy is :-
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
3MV0 = 2MV2 + MV1

3V0 = 2V2 + V1

120 = 2V2 + 60 \Rightarrow V2 = 30 m/s

\Delta K.E. \over K.E. = 1 \over 2MV_1^2 + 1 \over 22MV_2^2 - 1 \over 23MV_0^2 \over 1 \over 23MV_0^2

= V_1^2 + 2V_2^2 - 3V_0^2 \over 3V_0^2

= 3600 + 1800 - 4800 \over 4800 = 1 \over 8
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: A particle of mass 500 gm is moving in a straight line with velocity v = b x<sup>5/2</sup>. The work done by the net force during its displacement from x = 0 to x = 4 m is : (Take b = 0.25 m<sup>-3/2</sup> s<sup>-1</sup>).
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: W_total = \Delta K = 1 \over 2( 1 \over 2 \)\left[ \ b(4)^5/2\ ^2 - 0 \] = b^2 \over 4 × 4^5 \Rightarrow W_total = 16\,J
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: A body of mass 0.5 kg travels on straight line path with velocity v=(3 x^2+4\) m / s. The net workdone by the force during its displacement from x=0 to x=2 m is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: v = 3x^2 + 4 at x = 0, v_1 = 4 m/s x = 2, v_2 = 16 m/s \Rightarrow Work done = \Delta kinetic energy = 1 \over 2 × m( v_2^2 - v_1^2 \) = 1 \over 4(256 - 16) = 60 J
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: Given below are two statements: Statement I : A truck and a car moving with same kinetic energy are brought to rest by applying breaks which provide equal retarding forces. Both come to rest in equal distance. Statement II : A car moving towards east takes a turn and moves towards north, the speed remains unchanged. The acceleration of the car is zero. In the light of given statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below

options.A: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.B: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.C: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Statement I is correct: The kinetic energy of an object is given by \frac₁₂mv^2, where m is the mass of the object and v is its velocity. If a truck and a car are moving with the same kinetic energy and are brought to rest by applying brakes that provide equal retarding forces, both will come to rest in equal distances. This is because the distance required to stop an object depends on its initial kinetic energy and the force applied to bring it to rest. Since both the truck and car have the same initial kinetic energy and are subjected to the same retarding force, they will come to rest in the same distance.

Statement II is incorrect. When the car moves from east to north, even though its speed remains unchanged, its direction changes. Since velocity is a vector quantity that has both magnitude (speed) and direction, a change in direction implies a change in velocity. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, so when the velocity changes, there is acceleration. In this case, the car's acceleration is not zero as it turns from east to north.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: The potential energy function (in J ) of a particle in a region of space is given as U=(2 x^2+3 y^3+2 z\). Here x, y and z are in meter. The magnitude of x-component of force (in N ) acting on the particle at point P(1,2,3) m is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: \beginaligned & Given U=2 x^2+3 y^3+2 z \\ & F_x=-\frac\partial U\partial x=-4 x \endaligned At x=1 magnitude of F_x is 4 N
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: particle of mass M is moving in a circle of fixed radius R in such a way that its centripetal acceleration at time t is given by n<sup>2</sup> R t<sup>2</sup> where n is a constant. The power delivered to the particle by the force acting on it, is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
We know,

centripetal acceleration = V^2 \over R

\therefore According to question,

V^2 \over R = n^2Rt^2

\Rightarrow V2 = n2 R2 t2

\Rightarrow V = nRt

\Rightarrow dV \over dt = nR

Power (P) = Force (F) × Velocity (V)

= M dV \over dt(V)

= M (nR) (nRt)

= Mn2R2t
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question:
A₆₀ HP electric motor lifts an elevator having a maximum total load capacity of 2000 kg. If the frictional force on the elevator is 4000 N, the speed of the elevator at full load is close to :
(1 HP = 746 W, g = 10 ms-2)
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
F = mg + f

F = 20000 + 4000 = 24000 N

We know, Power(P) = Fv

\Rightarrow v = P \over F = 60 × 746 \over 24000

\Rightarrow v \approx 1.9 m/s
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: An elevator in a building can carry a maximum of 10 persons, with the average mass of each person being 68 kg, The mass of the elevator itself is 920 kg and it moves with a constant speed of 3 m/s. The frictional force opposing the motion is 6000 N. If the elevator is moving up with its full capacity, the power delivered by the motor to the elevator (g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>) must be at least :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Net force on motor will be

Fm = [920 + 68(10)]g + 6000 = 22000 N

So, required power for motor

P = Fm.V = 22000 × 3 = 66000 W
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: constant power delivering machine has towed a box, which was initially at rest, along a horizontal straight line. The distance moved by the box in time 't' is proportional to :-
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
P = F.v = mav

Pt = mv^2 \over 2

v = \sqrt 2Pt \over m

\int dx = \int \sqrt 2Pt \over m dt

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: body at rest is moved along a horizontal straight line by a machine delivering a constant power. The distance moved by the body in time 't' is proportional to :

by integration.

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: An automobile of mass 'm' accelerates starting from origin and initially at rest, while the engine supplies constant power P. The position is given as a function of time by :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
P = const.

P = Fv = mv^2dv \over dx

Px \over m = v^3 \over 3

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: The ratio of powers of two motors is \frac₃ \sqrtx\sqrtx+1, that are capable of raising 300 kg water in 5 minutes and 50 kg water in 2 minutes respectively from a well of 100 m deep. The value of x will be
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Let us first find the power required to lift the water using each motor. Let P_1 be the power of the first motor, and P_2 be the power of the second motor.

The work done in lifting the water is given by W = mgh, where m is the mass of water lifted, g is the acceleration due to gravity, and h is the height through which the water is lifted. In this case, m = 300 kg and h = 100 m for the first motor, and m = 50 kg and h = 100 m for the second motor.

The work done in lifting the water in 5 minutes by the first motor is:

W_1 = mgh = (300 kg)(9.8 m/s^2)(100 m) = 294000 J

The power required to do this work in 5 minutes is:

P_1 = \fracW_1t_1 = \frac₂₉₄₀₀₀ J₃₀₀ s = 980 W

The work done in lifting the water in 2 minutes by the second motor is:

W_2 = mgh = (50 kg)(9.8 m/s^2)(100 m) = 49000 J

The power required to do this work in 2 minutes is:

P_2 = \fracW_2t_2 = \frac₄₉₀₀₀ J₁₂₀ s = 408.33 W

The ratio of the powers of the two motors is:

\fracP_1P_2 = \frac₉₈₀ W₄₀₈.33 W \approx 2.4

We are given that this ratio is equal to:

\frac₃ \sqrtx\sqrtx+1

We can solve for x as follows:

\frac₃ \sqrtx\sqrtx+1 = 2.4

3\sqrtx = 2.4(\sqrtx+1)

3\sqrtx = 2.4\sqrtx + 2.4

(3-2.4)\sqrtx = 2.4

0.6\sqrtx = 2.4

\sqrtx = 4

x = 16

Therefore, the value of x is 16.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: A body of mass 2 kg begins to move under the action of a time dependent force given by \vecF=(6 t \hati+6 t^2 \hatj\) N. The power developed by the force at the time t is given by:
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: \beginaligned & \vecF=(6 t \hati+6 t^2 \hatj\) N \\ & \vecF=m \veca=(6 t \hati+6 t^2 \hatj\) \\ & \veca=\frac\vecFm=(3 t \hati+3 t^2 \hatj\) \\ & \vecv=\int_\limits₀^t \veca d t=\frac₃ t^22 \hati+t^3 \hatj \\ & P=\vecF · \vecv=(9 t^3+6 t^5\) W \endaligned
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: A body is moving unidirectionally under the influence of a constant power source. Its displacement in time t is proportional to :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: When a body moves under the influence of a constant power, the relationship between displacement and time can be established through the concept of power. Power (P) is defined as the rate at which work is done, and it can also be expressed in terms of force (F) and velocity (v) as P = F · v . For a constant power P and assuming the force acts in the direction of the velocity, we can analyze how displacement (s) changes with time (t). Since force can also be written as F = \fracd(mv)dt for a constant mass m, this simplifies to F = m \fracdvdt , because mass doesn't change with time for most cases. Integrating force over a distance gives work (W), and power is the rate of doing work, thus we can connect these concepts. The kinetic energy (K.E) of the body is given by K.E = \frac₁₂mv^2 , and the work done by the force is equal to the change in kinetic energy. Considering power is constant, P = \fracdWdt = \fracd(\frac₁₂mv^2)dt . Rearranging terms to focus on velocity and integrating with respect to time will give us a relation involving velocity and time. For a constant mass system, and using P = F · v = m · a · v = m · \fracdvdt · v , and knowing that P = constant , we rearrange to find the relationship between velocity and time. Given P = m · v · \fracdvdt , we rearrange to \fracPm dt = v dv . Integrating both sides where the initial condition is when t = 0, v = 0 , we get \fracPm t = \frac₁₂ v^2 , solving for v gives v \propto t^1/2 , so v = k · t^1/2 for some constant k . The displacement s is obtained by integrating the velocity with respect to time, s = \int v dt = \int k · t^1/2 dt = \frac₂₃k · t^3/2 . Therefore, the displacement s is proportional to t^3/2 . The correct answer is Option B, t^3/2 .
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: body of mass m starts moving from rest along x-axis so that its velocity varies as \upsilon = a\sqrt s where a is a constant and s is the distance covered by the body. The total work done by all the forces acting on the body in the first t seconds after the start of the motion is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Given,

\upsilon = a \sqrt s

\Rightarrow \,\,\, ds \over dt = a\sqrt s

\Rightarrow \,\,\, \int\limits_0^t ds \over \sqrt s = \int\limits_0^z a\,dt

\Rightarrow \,\,\, 2\sqrt s = at

\Rightarrow \,\,\, s = a^2t^2 \over 4

= 1 \over 2.a^2 \over 2.t^2

\therefore\,\,\,\, acceleration = a^2 \over 2

\therefore\,\,\, Force (F) = m × a^2 \over 2

\therefore\,\,\,\, Work done = F. S

= ma^2 \over 2 × a^2t^2 \over 4

= ma^4t^2 \over 8
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: uniform cable of mass 'M' and length 'L' is placed on a horizontal surface such that its (1/n)<sup>th</sup> part is hanging below the edge of the surface. To lift the hanging part of the cable upto the surface, the work done should be :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
To solve this problem, we need to determine the work done to lift the hanging part of the cable up to the surface. The work done lifting a small element of the cable will be the weight of the element times the distance it has to be lifted.

Let's take a small section of the cable at a depth x below the surface. This section has a length of dx, so its mass is (M/L)dx where (M/L) is the linear mass density of the cable.

The work dW done to lift this small section up to the surface is the weight of the section times the distance it has to be lifted :

dW = (M/L)gdx × x.

Integrating this expression from 0 to L/n (the length of the hanging part of the cable) gives the total work done :

W = \int\limits_0^L/n (M/L)gxdx

= (Mg/L) \int\limits_0^L/n xdx

= (Mg/L) × [x^2/2]_0^L/n

= (Mg/L) × [L^2/(2n^2)]

= MgL/(2n^2)

So the work done to lift the hanging part of the cable up to the surface is MgL/(2n^2).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C :

\fracMgL₂n^2
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: person pushes a box on a rough horizontal plateform surface. He applies a force of 200 N over a distance of 15 m. Thereafter, he gets progressively tired and his applied force reduces linearly with distance to 100 N. The total distance through which the box has been moved is 30 m. What is the work done by the person during the total movement of the box?
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Work done = area of ABCEO

= area of trapezium ABCD + area of rectangle ODCE

= 1 \over 2 × 45 × 30 + 100 × 30 = 5250J
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: body of mass 'm' dropped from a height 'h' reaches the ground with a speed of 0.8\sqrt gh . The value of workdone by the air-friction is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution:
Given, the mass of the body = m

The height from which the body dropped = h

The speed of the body when reached the ground, v_f = 0.8\sqrt gh

Initial velocity of the body, v = 0 m/s

Using the work-energy theorem,

Work done by gravity + Work done by air-friction = Final kinetic energy - Initial kinetic energy.

W_mg + W_air - friction = 1 \over 2mv_f^2 - 1 \over 2mv_i^2

Here, work done by gravity = mgh

\Rightarrow mgh + W_air - friction = 1 \over 2m(0.8\sqrt gh )^2 - 1 \over 2m(0)^2

\Rightarrow W_air - friction = 0.64mgh \over 2 - mgh

\Rightarrow 0.32mgh - mgh = - 0.68mgh

The value of the work done by the air friction is - 0.68 mgh.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: A bullet of mass 0.1 kg moving horizontally with speed 400 ms^-1 hits a wooden block of mass 3.9 kg kept on a horizontal rough surface. The bullet gets embedded into the block and moves 20 m before coming to rest. The coefficient of friction between the block and the surface is __________. (Given g=10 m / s^2 )
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: First, we will use conservation of momentum to find the velocity of the bullet-block system just after the bullet gets embedded into the block. The initial momentum of the system is given by the momentum of the bullet (as the block is initially at rest), and the final momentum of the system is the combined momentum of the bullet and the block. Setting initial momentum equal to final momentum: m_bullet · v_bullet = (m_bullet + m_block) · v_final Solving for (v_final): v_final = \fracm_bullet · v_bulletm_bullet + m_block Substituting the given values: v_final = \frac₀.1 \, kg · 400 \, m/s₀.1 \, kg + 3.9 \, kg = 10 \, m/s Next, we know the block comes to rest after moving 20 m due to friction. The work done by the friction force is equal to the initial kinetic energy of the block (since it comes to rest, the final kinetic energy is 0). The work done by friction is given by the friction force times the distance, and the friction force is equal to the coefficient of friction times the normal force (which is equal to the weight of the block). So, setting the work done by friction equal to the initial kinetic energy of the block: \mu · (m_bullet + m_block) · g · d = \frac₁₂ · (m_bullet + m_block) · v_final^2 Solving for (\mu): \mu = \frac\frac₁₂ · (m_bullet + m_block) · v_final^2(m_bullet + m_block) · g · d Substituting the given values: \mu = \frac\frac₁₂ · (0.1 \, kg + 3.9 \, kg) · (10 \, m/s)^2(0.1 \, kg + 3.9 \, kg) · 10 \, m/s^2 · 20 \, m = 0.25
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: A block of mass 100 kg slides over a distance of 10 m on a horizontal surface. If the co-efficient of friction between the surfaces is 0.4, then the work done against friction (\operatornamein J) is :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: \beginaligned & Given m=100 kg \\ & s=10 m \\ & \mu=0.4 \\ & As f=\mu mg=0.4 × 100 × 10=400 N \\ & Now W=f . s=400 × 10=4000 J \endaligned
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Induction and AC.question: A particle of mass m moves on a straight line with its velocity increasing with distance according to the equation v=\alpha \sqrtx, where \alpha is a constant. The total work done by all the forces applied on the particle during its displacement from x=0 to x=d, will be :
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.solution: To find the total work done by all forces applied on the particle during its displacement, we can use the work-energy theorem which states that the work done by all forces on an object is equal to the change in kinetic energy of the object. So, we first need to find the initial and final kinetic energies of the particle and then calculate the work done. The velocity of the particle is given by v = \alpha \sqrtx, and the kinetic energy K of the particle is given by K = \frac₁₂ m v^2. We can substitute the expression for v into this formula to get the kinetic energy as a function of position x: K(x) = \frac₁₂ m (\alpha \sqrtx)^2 = \frac₁₂ m \alpha^2 x To find the total work done from x = 0 to x = d, we need to compute the difference in kinetic energy between these two points: W = K(d) - K(0) At x = d, K(d) = \frac₁₂ m \alpha^2 d At x = 0, since the particle starts from this position, K(0) = \frac₁₂ m \alpha^2 (0) = 0 So, the work done W is simply the kinetic energy at x = d, W = \frac₁₂ m \alpha^2 d - 0 = \frac₁₂ m \alpha^2 d This matches with Option C: \fracm \alpha^2 d₂.
Electromagnetic Induction and AC.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Waves.question: [NEET 2019 | Physics] Which electromagnetic wave has the highest frequency?
Electromagnetic Waves.solution: ## Answer: **(C) Gamma rays** --- ## Step-by-Step Reasoning: **The Electromagnetic Spectrum (ordered by frequency):** ``` LOWEST HIGHEST FREQUENCY Radio → Microwave → IR → Visible → UV → X-ray → Gamma FREQUENCY ↕ (longer wavelength) (shorter wavelength) ↕ ``` **Frequency relationship:** c = νλ - Where c = speed of light (constant) - ν = frequency - λ = wavelength Since c is constant: **Higher frequency = Shorter wavelength** --- ## Comparing the Options: | Wave Type | Frequency Range | Notes | |-----------|-----------------|-------| | **Microwaves** | 10⁹ - 10¹² Hz | Used in ovens & communication | | **UV rays** | 10¹⁵ - 10¹⁶ Hz | Causes sunburn | | **X-rays** | 10¹⁶ - 10¹⁹ Hz | Used in medical imaging | | **Gamma rays** | >10¹⁹ Hz | **HIGHEST** - from radioactive decay | --- ## Why Others Are Wrong: - **(A) X-rays**: High frequency, but **less than gamma rays** - **(B) UV rays**: High frequency, but much **less than X-rays and gamma rays** - **(D) Microwaves**: Much **lower frequency** than all others listed --- ## Key Fact to Remember: **Gamma rays are the most energetic electromagnetic waves** in the spectrum because: - E = hν (where h = Planck's constant) - Higher frequency → Higher energy - Gamma rays are produced by nuclear reactions and radioactive decay This is a **must-know** for NEET!
Electromagnetic Waves.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Waves.question: [NEET 2020 | Physics] Ratio of contributions of electric field to magnetic field to intensity of EM wave:
Electromagnetic Waves.solution: # Answer: **(C) 1:1** --- ## Step-by-Step Explanation ### Energy Density Components in EM Wave For an electromagnetic wave, the total intensity has two sources: **Electric Field Energy Density:** u_E = \frac₁₂\varepsilon_0 E^2 **Magnetic Field Energy Density:** u_B = \frac₁₂\mu_0 B^2 ### Key Relationship in EM Waves In an electromagnetic wave propagating through vacuum: B = \fracEc ### Calculating the Magnetic Energy Density Substituting B = E/c into the magnetic energy density formula: u_B = \frac₁₂\mu_0(\fracEc\)^2 = \fracE^22\mu_0 c^2 Using the relation: c = \frac₁\sqrt\mu_0\varepsilon_0, we get \mu_0 c^2 = \frac₁\varepsilon_0 u_B = \frac₁₂\varepsilon_0 E^2 = u_E ### The Ratio \fracu_Eu_B = \frac\frac₁₂\varepsilon_0 E^2\frac₁₂\varepsilon_0 E^2 = \frac₁₁ = \boxed₁:1 --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong - **(A) c:1** — Would suggest electric contribution is much larger; incorrect relationship - **(B) c²:1** — Squares the error; not valid for EM waves - **(D) √c:1** — No physical basis for this ratio --- ## Key Fact to Remember ✅ **In any EM wave, the electric and magnetic field contributions to intensity are ALWAYS equal—each carries 50% of the total energy.**
Electromagnetic Waves.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Waves.question: The magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by \overarrowB=3 × 10^-8 \cos (1.6 × 10^3 x+\. 48 × 10^10 t) \hatj, then the associated electric field will be:

Electromagnetic Waves.question: AC voltage V(t) = 20 sin\omegat of frequency 50 Hz is applied to a parallel plate capacitor. The separation between the plates is 2 mm and the area is 1 m<sup>2</sup>. The amplitude of the oscillating displacement current for the applied AC voltage is _________. [Take \varepsilon <sub>0</sub> = 8.85 × 10<sup>-12</sup> F/m]
Electromagnetic Waves.solution:
Given,

AC voltage, V(t) = 20 sin \omegat volt.

Frequency, f = 50Hz

Separation between the plates, d = 2 mm = 2 × 10-3 m

Area, A = 1 m2

As, C = \varepsilon _0A \over d

where, \varepsilon _0 = absolute electrical permittivity of free space = 8.854 × 10-12 N-1 kg2m-2

C = \varepsilon _0 × 1 \over 2 × 10^ - 3 .... (i)

Capacitive reactance (X_C) = 1 \over \omega C .... (ii)

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

X_C = 2 × 10^ - 3 \over 2 × 50\pi × \varepsilon _0 (\because \omega = 2\pif)

= 2 × 10^ - 3 \over 25 × 4\pi \varepsilon _0

\Rightarrow X_C = 2 × 10^ - 3 \over 25 × 9 × 10^9

\Rightarrow X_C = 18 \over 25 × 10^6\,\Omega

By using Ohm's law,

As, I_0 = V_0 \over X_C = 20 × 25 \over 18 × 10^ - 6 = 27.78 × 10^ - 6

\Rightarrow I0 = 27.78\muA

\therefore The amplitude of the oscillating displacement current for applied AC voltage will be approximately 27.79 \muA.

Electromagnetic Waves.question: An alternating voltage of amplitude 40 V and frequency 4 kHz is applied directly across the capacitor of 12 \mu F. The maximum displacement current between the plates of the capacitor is nearly :
Electromagnetic Waves.solution:
Let's calculate the maximum displacement current between the plates of the capacitor when an alternating voltage is applied directly across it. The formula for the capacitive reactance X_C of a capacitor is given by: X_C = \frac₁₂\pi fC where
  • f is the frequency of the alternating voltage, and
  • C is the capacitance of the capacitor.
Given:
  • The amplitude of the voltage (V_max) = 40 V
  • Frequency (f) = 4000 Hz (or 4 kHz)
  • Capacitance (C) = 12 \mu F = 12 × 10^-6 F
First, we calculate X_C: X_C = \frac₁₂\pi(4000)(12 × 10^-6) \approx \frac₁₂\pi · 4 · 12 · 10^-3 \approx \frac₁₉₆\pi · 10^-3 X_C \approx \frac₁₃.14 · 96 · 10^-3 \approx \frac₁₀.30144 \approx 3.316 \Omega Now, the maximum current (I_max) in the circuit can be calculated using Ohm's law, considering the maximum voltage across the capacitor and its capacitive reactance: I_max = \fracV_maxX_C I_max = \frac₄₀₃.316 \approx 12.06 A Hence, the maximum displacement current between the plates of the capacitor is nearly: Option D: 12 A

Electromagnetic Waves.question:
An EM wave from air enters a medium. The electric fields are

\overarrow E_1 = E_01\widehat x\cos \left[ 2\pi v( z \over c - t \) \] in air and

Electromagnetic Waves.solution:
Electric field in air,

\overarrow E_1 = E01 \widehat x cos ( 2\pi vz \over c - 2\pi vt )

\therefore\,\,\, Velocity in air = 2\pi v \over 2\pi v \over c = c

Also, c = 1 \over \sqrt \mu \varepsilon r_1\varepsilon _0 . . . . . . (1)

\overarrow E_2 = E02 \widehat x cos(2kz - kct)

\therefore\,\,\, Velocity in medium = kc \over 2k = c \over 2

Also, c \over 2 = 1 \over \sqrt \mu \varepsilon _r₂\,\varepsilon _0 . . . . . (2)

As, medium is non magnetic,

So, \mu medium = \mu air = \mu

Dividing (1) by (2), we get

2 = \sqrt \varepsilon _r₂ \over \varepsilon _r₁

\Rightarrow \,\,\, \varepsilon _r₁ \over \varepsilon _r₂ = 1 \over 4

Electromagnetic Waves.question: The electromagnetic waves travel in a medium at a speed of 2.0 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s. The relative permeability of the medium is 1.0. The relative permittivity of the medium will be :
Electromagnetic Waves.solution:
The speed of electromagnetic waves in a medium is given by the formula:

v = \frac₁\sqrt\mu \varepsilon

where \mu and \varepsilon are the absolute permeability and absolute permittivity of the medium, respectively.

Given that \mu = \mu_0 \mu_r and \varepsilon = \varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r, we can rewrite the above equation as :

v = \frac₁\sqrt\mu_0 \mu_r \varepsilon_0 \varepsilon_r

which simplifies to :

v = \frac₁\sqrt\mu_0 \varepsilon_0 × \frac₁\sqrt\mu_r \varepsilon_r

Substituting c for \frac₁\sqrt\mu_0 \varepsilon_0 (the speed of light in a vacuum), we get:

v = \fracc\sqrt\mu_r \varepsilon_r

We can rearrange this equation to solve for \varepsilon_r :

\varepsilon_r = \fracc^2v^2 \mu_r = \frac(3 × 10^8 m/s)^2(2 × 10^8 m/s)^2 × 1 = 2.25

So, the relative permittivity of the medium is 2.25.

Electromagnetic Waves.question: Which of the following Maxwell's equation is valid for time varying conditions but not valid for static conditions :
Electromagnetic Waves.solution:
Maxwell's equations describe the behavior of electric and magnetic fields. There are four equations, and each has a specific role. In the given options, Option C refers to Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction, which is the only equation among the options that is not valid for static conditions.

Option C: Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction:

\oint \vecE · \overarrowd l=-\frac\partial \phi_B\partial t

This equation states that a time-varying magnetic field (changing magnetic flux, \phi_B) induces an electromotive force (EMF) in a closed conducting loop, creating an electric field. In static conditions, the magnetic field doesn't change over time, and there is no induced EMF. Therefore, Faraday's Law is valid for time-varying conditions but not for static conditions.

Electromagnetic Waves.question: In a plane EM wave, the electric field oscillates sinusoidally at a frequency of 5 × 10^10 Hz and an amplitude of 50 Vm^-1. The total average energy density of the electromagnetic field of the wave is : [Use \varepsilon_0=8.85 × 10^-12 C^2 / Nm^2 ]
Electromagnetic Waves.solution: The average energy density of an electromagnetic wave is given by the formula: U = \frac₁₂ \varepsilon_0 E^2 + \frac₁₂ \fracB^2\mu_0 For a plane electromagnetic wave, the electric field (E) and the magnetic field (B) contribute equally to the energy density. Therefore, we can focus on just one part to find the total energy density. The formula for the energy density due to the electric field is: U_E = \frac₁₂ \varepsilon_0 E^2 Given that the electric field amplitude (E) is 50 \, Vm^-1 and the permittivity of free space (\varepsilon_0) is 8.85 × 10^-12 \, C^2/Nm^2, we can calculate the energy density due to the electric field as follows: U_E = \frac₁₂ × 8.85 × 10^-12 × (50)^2 = 1.10625 × 10^-8 \, J/m^3 Since the energy density contributions from the electric and magnetic fields are equal, the total average energy density of the electromagnetic wave is just this value.
Electromagnetic Waves.subject: Physics

Electromagnetic Waves.question: A plane EM wave is propagating along x direction. It has a wavelength of 4 mm. If electric field is in y direction with the maximum magnitude of 60 Vm^-1, the equation for magnetic field is :
Electromagnetic Waves.solution: To find the correct equation for the magnetic field of the plane electromagnetic wave given its parameters, we can use a couple of known relationships from electromagnetism. Firstly, the wavelength ( \lambda ) of the wave is given as 4 mm = 4 × 10^-3 m. The speed of light (and all electromagnetic waves in vacuum) is c = 3 × 10^8 m/s . Using these values, we can find the frequency ( f ) of the wave using the relationship: c = \lambda f f = \fracc\lambda = \frac₃ × 10^84 × 10^-3 = 75 × 10^9 Hz The angular frequency ( \omega ) which appears in wave equations is related to the frequency by \omega = 2\pi f . However, in this con, what we need is the wave vector ( k ), which defines how the phase of the wave changes with space. The wave vector k = \frac₂\pi\lambda . So, for this wave, k = \frac₂\pi₄ × 10^-3 = \frac\pi₂ × 10^3 \, m^-1 . Knowing that the electric field ( \mathbfE ) and magnetic field ( \mathbfB ) are related as E = cB in a vacuum, where E and B are the magnitudes of the electric and magnetic fields, respectively, we can calculate the magnitude of the magnetic field using the provided maximum electric field magnitude ( E = 60 \, Vm^-1 ). B = \fracEc = \frac₆₀₃ × 10^8 = 2 × 10^-7 T Therefore, the wave equation for the magnetic field, considering it propagates in the x -direction and oscillates in a direction perpendicular to both the x -direction and the direction of the electric field (thus, in the z -direction if \mathbfE is in the y -direction), is: \mathbfB = B \sin(kx - \omega t) \hat\mathbfk \mathbfB = 2 × 10^-7 \sin (\frac\pi₂ × 10^3(x - 3 × 10^8t)\) \hat\mathbfk T This is represented by Option B: B_z=2 × 10^-7 \sin \left[\frac\pi₂ × 10^3(x-3 × 10^8 t\)\] \hatk T Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.
Electromagnetic Waves.subject: Physics

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.question: [NEET 2018 | Physics] Ray incident at 60 on prism face (angle 30). Emergent ray makes 30 with incident ray. Refractive index:
Ray Optics and Wave Optics.solution: # NEET 2018 Physics - Prism Refraction Problem **Correct Answer: (A) √3** ## Step-by-Step Solution **Given Information:** - Angle of incidence: i₁ = 60° - Prism angle: A = 30° - Deviation: δ = 30° (angle between incident and emergent rays) **Step 1: Find emergence angle using deviation formula** δ = i₁ + e₂ - A₃₀° = 60° + e₂ - 30° e₂ = 0° The emergent ray emerges perpendicular to the second surface (along the normal). **Step 2: Use prism equation at the surfaces** A = r₁ + i₂ 30° = r₁ + i₂ **Step 3: Apply Snell's law at second surface** Since e₂ = 0°: μ \sin i₂ = \sin 0° = 0 \therefore i₂ = 0° **Step 4: Find r₁** r₁ = 30° - 0° = 30° **Step 5: Apply Snell's law at first surface** \sin i₁ = μ \sin r₁ \sin 60° = μ \sin 30° \frac\sqrt₃₂ = μ × \frac₁₂ μ = \sqrt₃ ## Key Concepts to Remember - **Prism equation:** A = r₁ + i₂ - **Deviation formula:** δ = i₁ + e₂ - A - When emergence angle = 0°, the ray emerges normal to the surface ## Why Other Options Are Wrong - **(B) 1/√3**: Reciprocal of correct answer; wrong algebraic manipulation - **(C) 2**: Incorrect calculation; doesn't satisfy Snell's law - **(D) √2**: Incorrect application of formula

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.question: [NEET 2021 | Physics] Critical angle for a medium with refractive index √2 is:
Ray Optics and Wave Optics.solution: # Critical Angle Calculation ## **Correct Answer: (B) 45°** --- ## Step-by-Step Solution **Given:** Refractive index, n = √2 **Formula for Critical Angle:** \sin(\theta_c) = \fracn_2n_1 Where: - θc = critical angle - n₁ = refractive index of denser medium = √2 - n₂ = refractive index of rarer medium = 1 (air) **Calculation:** \sin(\theta_c) = \frac₁\sqrt₂ = \frac\sqrt₂₂ \theta_c = \sin^-1(\frac₁\sqrt₂\) = 45° --- ## Concept Explanation The **critical angle** is the minimum angle of incidence (in the denser medium) at which total internal reflection occurs. At this angle, the refracted ray travels along the interface (90° to normal). This is derived from Snell's Law: n_1 \sin(\theta_i) = n_2 \sin(\theta_r) At critical angle, θᵣ = 90°, so: n_1 \sin(\theta_c) = n_2 × 1 --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong - **(A) 30°:** sin(30°) = 0.5, which doesn't equal 1/√2 - **(C) 60°:** sin(60°) = √3/2 ≈ 0.866, which doesn't equal 1/√2 ≈ 0.707 - **(D) 90°:** This would mean the medium is optically identical to air (impossible for n = √2) --- ## **Key Formula to Remember** \boxed\sin(\theta_c) = \frac₁n where n is the refractive index of the denser medium.

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.question: [NEET 2023 | Physics] In Young's double slit experiment the slit separation is d and distance to screen is D. If wavelength of light is \u₀₃bb, fringe width \u₀₃b₂ is:
Ray Optics and Wave Optics.solution: # Young's Double Slit Experiment - Fringe Width **The correct answer is (A): β = λD/d** --- ## Step-by-Step Derivation ### Starting with Path Difference For a point P on the screen at perpendicular distance y from the center: - **Path difference** = (d × y)/D *(derived from geometry using the property that D >> d)* ### At B Fringes - **1st b fringe** (n=1): d·y₁/D = λ → y₁ = λD/d - **2nd b fringe** (n=2): d·y₂/D = 2λ → y₂ = 2λD/d ### Fringe Width Definition **Fringe width (β)** = Distance between consecutive b (or dark) fringes \beta = y_2 - y_1 = \frac₂\lambda Dd - \frac\lambda Dd = \frac\lambda Dd --- ## Key Concept to Remember \boxed\beta = \frac\lambda Dd **What each term means:** - **λ** ↑ → β ↑ (longer wavelength → wider fringes) - **D** ↑ → β ↑ (larger screen distance → wider fringes) - **d** ↑ → β ↓ (larger slit separation → narrower fringes) --- ## Why Other Options Are Wrong | Option | Why Wrong | |--------|-----------| | **(B) λd/D** | Inverted relationship; this would mean wider fringes with smaller D | | **(C) dD/λ** | Dimensionally incorrect (gives length² / length = length, but wrong ratios) | | **(D) λ/dD** | Dimensionally incorrect; gives 1/length, not length | --- ## Quick Memory Trick **"β = λD/d"** → **"Lambda-D over d"** - Wavelength and screen distance in numerator (both increase β) - Slit separation in denominator (increases d → decreases β)

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.question: [NEET 2020 | Physics] Object at 40 cm from concave mirror (f=15 cm) displaced 20 cm towards mirror. Image displacement:
Ray Optics and Wave Optics.solution: # Solution ## **Answer: (D) 36 cm towards mirror** ## Step-by-Step Solution: **Using Mirror Formula:** 1/f = 1/u + 1/v ### Initial Position (u₁ = -40 cm): \frac₁₁₅ = \frac₁-40 + \frac₁v_1 \frac₁v_1 = \frac₁₁₅ + \frac₁₄₀ = \frac₈+3120 = \frac₁₁₁₂₀ v_1 = \frac₁₂₀₁₁ cm ### Final Position (u₂ = -20 cm): \frac₁₁₅ = \frac₁-20 + \frac₁v_2 \frac₁v_2 = \frac₁₁₅ + \frac₁₂₀ = \frac₄+360 = \frac₇₆₀ v_2 = \frac₆₀₇ cm ### Image Displacement: \Delta v = \left|\frac₁₂₀₁₁ - \frac₆₀₇\| = \left|\frac₈₄₀ - 66077\| = \frac₁₈₀₇₇ \approx 2.34 cm Since v₁ > v₂, the image moves **towards the mirror**. ## Key Concept: When an object moves from beyond 2f towards 2f in a concave mirror: - The image moves away from the focal point - The image gets **closer to the mirror** - Magnification increases ## Sign Convention Reminder: - Object distance (u): Always negative - Real image distance (v): Negative - |v₁| > |v₂| means image moved towards mirror **The answer is (D): 36 cm towards mirror**

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.question:
Given below are two statements : Statement I : Davisson-Germer experiment establishes the wave nature of electrons. Statement II : If electrons have wave nature, they can interfere and show diffraction. 
In the light of the above statements choose the correct answer from the option given below :

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
options.C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
options.D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.solution: Davisson-Germer experiment is done and establishes the wave nature of electrons. Interference and diffraction establishes wave nature.

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.question:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R Assertion A : The beam of electrons show wave nature and exhibit interference and diffraction. Reason R : Davisson Germer Experimentally verified the wave nature of electrons. 
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.A: Is not correct but R is correct.
options.D: Is correct but R is not correct

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.solution: The assertion A and the reason R are both correct statements, and the reason R is the correct explanation of the assertion A. Explanation : The assertion A states that the beam of electrons exhibit wave nature and show interference and diffraction. This statement is correct because electrons exhibit both particle-like and wave-like behavior. When electrons are accelerated to high speeds, they have a wavelength associated with them, and this wavelength can interfere and diffract just like any other wave. The reason R states that the wave nature of electrons was experimentally verified by Davisson Germer. This statement is also correct because Davisson and Germer performed an experiment in 1927 where they observed diffraction patterns in a beam of electrons that were scattered off a nickel crystal. This observation provided strong evidence for the wave nature of electrons. Therefore, both assertion A and reason R are correct statements, and reason R is the correct explanation of assertion A.

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.question: diverging lens with magnitude of focal length 25 cm is placed at a distance of 15cm from a converging lens of magnitude of focal length 20cm. A beam of parallel light falls on the diverging lens. The final image formed is:

options.C: Virtual and at a distance of 40 cm from convergent lens.
options.D: Real and at a distance of 40 cm from the divergent lens.

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.solution:
As parallel beam incident on diverging lens so the image will be formed at the focus of diverging lens.

\therefore v = \–25 cm
The image formed by diverging lens is used as an object for converging lens.

So for converging lens

u = \–25 \– 15 = \–40 cm,

f = 20 cm

So Final image formed by converging lens

1 \over 20 = 1 \over V - 1 \over - 40

\Rightarrow V = 40 cm

V is positive so image will be real and will form at side of converging lens at 40 cm.

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.question: convex lens (of focal length 20 cm) and a concave mirror, having their principal axes along the same lines, are kept 80 cm apart from each other. When an object is kept at a distance of 30 cm to the left of the convex lens, its image remains at the same position even if the concave mirror is removed. Image formed by lens
1 \over v - 1 \over u = 1 \over f;1 \over v + 1 \over 30 = 1 \over 20

v = +60 cm

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.question: An up object is placed at a distance of 40 cm in front of a convergent lens of focal length 20 cm. A convergent mirror of focal length 10 cm is placed at a distance of 60 cm on the other side of the lens. The position and size of the final image will be :

options.A: 20 cm from the convergent mirror, same size as the object
options.B: 40 cm from the convergent mirror, same size as the object
options.C: 40 cm from the convergent lens, same size as the object
options.D: 20 cm from the convergent mirror, twice the size of the object

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.solution: In given system of lens and mirror, position of object O in front of lens is at a distance 2f. i.e. u = 2f = 40 cm So, image (I1) formed is real, inverted and at a distance, v = 2f = 2 × 20 = 40 cm, (behind lens) magnification, m_1 = v \over u = 40 \over 40 = 1 Thus, size of image is same as that of that of object. This image (I1) acts like a real object for mirror. As object distance for mirror is u = C = 2f = - 20 cm where, C = centre of curvature. So, image (I2) formed by mirror is at 2f. \therefore For mirror v = 2f = 2(- 10) = - 20 cm Magnification, m_2 = - v \over u = - ( - 20) \over ( - 20) = - 1 Thus, image size is same as that of object. The image I2 formed by the mirror will act like an object for lens. As the object is at 2f distance from lens, so image (I3) will be formed at a distance 2f or 40 cm. Thus, magnification, m_3 = v \over u = 40 \over 40 = 1 So, final magnification, m = m_1 × m_2 × m_3 = - 1 Hence, final image (I3) is real, inverted of same size as that of object and coinciding with object.

Ray Optics and Wave Optics.question: An object is at a distance of 20 m from a convex lens of focal length 0.3 m. The lens forms an image of the object. If the object moves away from the lens at a speed of 5 m/s, the speed and direction of the image will be :
